newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Milosevic praises police over Kosovo action.
newsitem.headline: Milosevic praises police over Kosovo action.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic congratulated leading interior ministry officials on Monday following a successful "anti-terrorist operation" in the Kosovo province late last month, Tanjug news agency said.
Milosevic met Serbian Interior Minister Zoran Sokolovic, Public Security chief Colonel-General Radovan Stojicic and State Security chief Jovica Stanisic to discuss the operation.

The operation took place between January 22 and 29 and resulted in the arrests of 66 "members of terrorist organisations ... among them perpetrators of terrorist acts carried out in Kosovo," Tanjug said.
Milosevic paid tribute to the Serbian Interior Ministry for a successful operation, the agency said.

Milosevic said the people of Kosovo, regardless of their nationality, had the right to live in freedom and peace and resolve political issues by political means, publicly and democratically, without pressure and fear from violence.
Serbian police had shot dead three Albasnians in a gunbattle on Friday as part of an operation aimed at stamping out terrorism in Kosovo, Tanjug said.
A suspected commander of the outlawed Liberation Army of Kosovo was among the three men killed.
The agency identified the guerrilla suspect as 34-year-old Zahir Pajaziti. Police were shot at and returned fire, it said.

The Democratic League, Kosovo's biggest ethnic Albanian party, said it condemned the killings. In describing the incident, it made no mention of any political or guerrilla affiliation of the three ethnic Albanians who died.
The clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army is reported to have been behind several guerrilla attacks over the past year in which both ethnic Albanians loyal to Belgrade and Serbians have died.

In 1989 Serbia's autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic removed Albania's autonomous status, accusing the Albanian majority of preparing to secede. Ever since the province has been widely seen as a powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
